query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: The type of issue is a common cause of both how a ticket is routed/handled (treatment) and how long it takes to resolve (outcome). It is a pre-existing property not named in the query, so it functions as a confounder that must be adjusted for.

per_column.name: estimated_complexity
per_column.rationale: Intrinsic difficulty of the ticket drives both routing/escalation decisions and resolution time. It is a common cause not intervenable by the actor and not named in the query, so it is a confounder.

per_column.name: routing_recommendation
per_column.rationale: Routing/escalation is an action a support team can actually SET or DECIDE (escalate, handle first-tier, route to a specialist). This is a settable lever whose effect on resolution time is the interventional question.

per_column.name: self_service_candidate
per_column.rationale: Whether to divert a ticket to self-service is a decidable operational lever the team could set, making it an intervenable treatment on resolution time.

judge.rationale: The 'reduce resolution time' query is genuinely interventional. The added set includes at least one true intervenable treatment (routing_recommendation, and arguably self_service_candidate) that a support team can actually decide, satisfying part (a). It also supplies two solid common causes of both the routing decision and resolution time (issue_category, estimated_complexity), neither of which was named or implied in the query, satisfying part (b) and demonstrating the confounder-discovery capability. These are pre-treatment attributes, not mediators or colliders. The set thus realises the what-if claim well, though it omits some plausible confounders like agent skill/tenure and current queue load.
